result.title: Can the Remaining Answers Change the Prediction? Worst-Case Stability Checks for Personalized Rating Models
result.summary: Missing ratings can overturn a personalized model's current prediction. For completed models with additive response scores, exact worst case bounds check all missing assignments without changing the current predictor. We evaluate this audit retrospectively in two self-triage cohorts, 108 clinicians rating three simulated psychiatric interviews, and 126 counseling demonstrations annotated by ten experts. Under shared random half histories, Fisher adaptation based on observed ratings reduces log loss relative to response frequency by 0.1071 nats in the clinician audit (95% CI [0.0867,0.1261]) and 0.0223 in counseling (95% CI[0.0121,0.0321]). The counseling test excludes target experts and source videos from training. Certification covers 5.4% and 10.5% of targets; fixed width acquisition raises coverage to 13.7% and 28.6% at the same budgets. With weights and responses held fixed, the observed-rating update also has lower loss than an affine partial update while certifying exactly the same evaluated targets. The certificate establishes agreement with the completed model, not correctness or stability at intermediate updates. These rating tasks test the method; clinical usefulness remains untested.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对可加响应分数的个性化评分模型，提出无需改动现有预测器即可遍历所有缺失赋值的精确最坏情况界，用以检验缺失评分是否会翻转当前预测，并在两个专家标注队列上回顾性审计该证书，比较 Fisher 适应更新与固定宽度采集的覆盖率与损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 用最坏情况界在证据缺失时认证预测稳定性、并权衡固定预算下的证据采集覆盖率，可能与 LVR 中停止决策、视觉证据筛选及中间状态更新的稳定性评价存在概念联系，其证书框架能否迁移至 latent 状态可供核查。
